plain_english: A running total of volume that adds on up-days and subtracts on down-days. Rising OBV while price stalls often means hidden accumulation; falling OBV while price rises often means distribution.
one_line_example: Price broke out but OBV slope was flat — classic warning of a fake breakout.

plain_english: When price and an indicator (OBV, RSI, MACD) move in opposite directions — often a leading signal of a trend change.
one_line_example: RSI made a lower high while price made a higher high — bearish divergence.

plain_english: Price closing decisively above a resistance level or trendline, often on elevated volume.
one_line_example: Stock broke out above its 200-day moving average on 3× normal volume.

plain_english: Illegal parallel trading outside regulated exchanges. Orders are matched off-book by operators.
one_line_example: Dabba brokers offer leverage retail can't get on Zerodha but have zero protection if things go wrong.

plain_english: Slang for a stock being actively driven by a coordinated group pumping price before distributing to retail.
one_line_example: That small-cap doubled in two weeks with no news — classic operator play.

plain_english: Risk-adjusted return: excess return over risk-free rate divided by volatility. Higher is better.
one_line_example: Strategy A has 15% returns but Sharpe of 0.5; Strategy B has 12% with Sharpe 1.2 — B is the better risk-adjusted bet.

plain_english: How much a stock moves relative to the market. Beta of 1.5 means the stock tends to move 1.5× the Nifty.
one_line_example: High-beta stocks rally harder in up-markets but crater harder in corrections.

plain_english: Cash left for shareholders after capex and debt servicing — what the company could theoretically return as dividends.
one_line_example: Strong reported earnings but negative FCFE — the profits exist on paper but can't be distributed.

plain_english: The rate at which RBI lends to banks. Higher repo rate → loans get costlier across the economy.
one_line_example: RBI hiked repo by 25bps, so EMIs on new home loans will tick up.

plain_english: RBI buying or selling government bonds to inject or drain liquidity from the banking system.
one_line_example: RBI announced ₹40,000 cr OMO purchases — that's a liquidity injection into banks.

plain_english: Minimum percentage of bank deposits banks must hold in government-approved securities.
one_line_example: If SLR is cut, banks have more cash to lend.

plain_english: Share of deposits banks must hold as cash with RBI. Directly controls how much banks can lend.
one_line_example: CRR cut by 50bps = about ₹1.1 lakh crore freed up for lending.

plain_english: The strike price at which the total value of expiring options is minimized — often a magnet for price on expiry day.
one_line_example: Max pain sits at 22500 Nifty, so gravitation towards that level on expiry is expected.

plain_english: Total outstanding option or futures contracts not yet settled. Rising OI with rising price = long build-up; rising OI with falling price = short build-up.
one_line_example: Call OI at 22000 doubled in two sessions — resistance is getting serious.

plain_english: Put-Call Ratio of open interest. PCR > 1 signals bearish positioning; PCR < 0.7 signals bullish positioning.
one_line_example: Nifty PCR dropped to 0.6 — traders are positioned heavily long.

plain_english: SEBI rules that require disclosure whenever a person crosses 5% shareholding or changes holding by 2% in a listed company.
one_line_example: SAST filing just showed the promoter bought another 1.5% — insider conviction signal.

plain_english: SEBI regulation governing insider-trading disclosures. Designated persons must disclose all share transactions within 2 days.
one_line_example: PIT disclosure showed the CFO sold 80% of his ESOPs the week before the earnings miss.

plain_english: A capital raise where a listed company sells shares only to institutional investors — faster than a public issue.
one_line_example: Company announced a ₹1,500 cr QIP at a 4% discount — near-term supply overhang.

plain_english: Promoter has borrowed against their shares. High pledge is a red flag — lenders can force-sell if price falls.
one_line_example: Promoter pledge jumped from 15% to 40% in a quarter — margin call risk just went up.

plain_english: Foreign funds investing in Indian markets. Their net buying/selling moves the broader indices.
one_line_example: FIIs sold ₹8,000 cr in cash market — that's what dragged Nifty down.

plain_english: Indian mutual funds + insurance companies + pension funds. Typically absorb FII outflows during corrections.
one_line_example: FIIs sold ₹5,000 cr but DIIs bought ₹6,500 cr — net positive.

plain_english: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization — a proxy for operating profitability before capital structure effects.
one_line_example: EBITDA margin expanded 300bps YoY — operational leverage is kicking in.

plain_english: Net profit divided by number of outstanding shares. Higher EPS = more profit per share you own.
one_line_example: EPS grew 25% YoY but the stock is flat — re-rating opportunity.

plain_english: Price per share divided by EPS — how many years of current earnings it'd take to recoup the share price.
one_line_example: Stock trades at 12× P/E vs sector 18× — either bargain or value trap.

plain_english: Per-stock daily price band set by the exchange. Hitting upper/lower circuit freezes trading in one direction.
one_line_example: Stock hit upper circuit for 5 straight sessions — retail getting locked in.

plain_english: Daily end-of-day data file published by NSE/BSE containing OHLC, volume, delivery % for every scrip.
one_line_example: Pull the bhavcopy to compute delivery % trends for the screener.

plain_english: Share of traded volume that resulted in actual stock delivery vs intraday unwinds. High delivery % = conviction buying/selling.
one_line_example: Delivery % spiked to 80% on huge volume — someone is accumulating with real money.

plain_english: Buying or selling shares using material non-public information. Illegal. The public PIT disclosures are the legal disclosure track for designated persons.
one_line_example: Two directors bought in a quiet window — PIT filing incoming.

plain_english: India's main benchmark index — the 50 largest NSE-listed stocks.
one_line_example: Nifty up 120 pts today driven by HDFC Bank and Reliance.

plain_english: BSE's 30-stock benchmark index — the Indian market's other flagship.
one_line_example: Sensex crossed 80,000 for the first time.

plain_english: Index of the 12 most liquid banking stocks. The most-traded F&O underlying in India.
one_line_example: Bank Nifty rolled over 15% of OI to next series — positioning is getting heavy.

plain_english: The derivatives segment — futures and options contracts on stocks and indices.
one_line_example: Stock got added to F&O ban list — new positions blocked until OI drops.

plain_english: The day a derivatives contract settles. Weekly Nifty/Bank Nifty expiries are Thursday; monthly last Thursday.
one_line_example: Heavy premium decay entering expiry day — writers benefit.

plain_english: India VIX — expected 30-day Nifty volatility implied from option prices. Rising VIX = fear; falling VIX = complacency.
one_line_example: VIX spiked to 22 from 13 in a week — market pricing in risk.

plain_english: Carrying futures positions from current expiry to next by closing current and opening in next series.
one_line_example: Nifty rollover at 75% — in line with the three-month average.

plain_english: Return in excess of what the market's risk profile would predict — the skill component of returns.
one_line_example: Fund generated 4% alpha over the index adjusted for beta.

plain_english: Peak-to-trough decline of a portfolio. Tells you the worst dip a strategy has historically survived.
one_line_example: Max drawdown of 18% — manageable for a long-only equity strategy.

plain_english: How much returns fluctuate around the mean. Often annualized as standard deviation of daily returns.
one_line_example: Realized vol collapsed to 9% — Bollinger squeeze ahead of breakout.

plain_english: Price level where supply (sellers) historically overwhelms demand and halts rallies.
one_line_example: 22500 is major resistance; a clean break opens upside to 23000.

plain_english: Price level where demand (buyers) historically overwhelms supply and halts declines.
one_line_example: Stock bounced off 450 support — sixth time this year.

plain_english: The individuals/entities that founded or control a listed company. Their shareholding and pledge patterns are leading signals.
one_line_example: Promoter stake dropped 4% in the quarter without disclosed sale reason — watch out.

plain_english: New share issuance that reduces existing shareholders' ownership percentage. Can be via FPO, QIP, preferential allotment, warrants.
one_line_example: 20% dilution via QIP — expect near-term pressure.

plain_english: Company buying back its own shares from the market, usually signalling cash strength or that management thinks shares are undervalued.
one_line_example: ₹4,000 cr buyback at 12% premium — floor under the stock for the buyback window.

plain_english: Cash distribution to shareholders. Ex-date is when you need to own the stock to be entitled.
one_line_example: Interim dividend of ₹8 with ex-date next Tuesday.

plain_english: The date from which new buyers are NOT entitled to the announced dividend. Stock typically opens lower by the dividend amount.
one_line_example: Stock dropped 2% on ex-date — that's just the dividend adjustment, not weakness.

plain_english: The date on which a company looks at its shareholder register to decide who gets the corporate action (dividend, bonus, split).
one_line_example: Bonus record date 15th — need to be on the register by then.

plain_english: Free additional shares given to existing shareholders in a ratio. Doesn't change your % ownership but increases share count.
one_line_example: 1:1 bonus — you'll have twice as many shares at half the price.

plain_english: Reduction of face value that multiplies share count proportionally — purely cosmetic, total market cap unchanged.
one_line_example: 1:5 split — each share of ₹10 face value becomes 5 shares of ₹2 face value.

plain_english: Taking an offsetting position to reduce risk of an existing position — e.g. long cash + short futures.
one_line_example: Hedged my portfolio with Nifty puts before the Fed meeting.

plain_english: Simultaneously exploiting price differences of the same asset across markets/instruments for low-risk profit.
one_line_example: Cash-futures arb narrows when funding costs rise.

plain_english: Bombay Stock Exchange — Asia's oldest stock exchange.
one_line_example: BSE corporate filings are the fastest official disclosure source.

plain_english: National Stock Exchange — India's largest exchange by volume.
one_line_example: NSE accounts for ~95% of equity volume vs BSE.

plain_english: Securities and Exchange Board of India — the market regulator.
one_line_example: SEBI tightened disclosure norms for F&O stocks.

plain_english: Reserve Bank of India — the central bank. Sets the repo rate, manages currency, regulates banks.
one_line_example: RBI's MPC held rates steady for the seventh time.

plain_english: The six-member RBI committee that sets the repo rate and monetary policy stance.
one_line_example: MPC minutes showed a 4-2 vote to hold — internal split on inflation.

plain_english: Initial Public Offering — a company's first sale of shares to public investors.
one_line_example: IPO subscribed 80× in QIB, 5× in retail — premium on listing day likely.

plain_english: Follow-on Public Offering — a listed company selling more shares to the public.
one_line_example: FPO priced at 8% discount to market — dilutive near-term.

plain_english: Unofficial premium at which IPO shares trade in the grey market before listing. Proxy for listing-day expectations.
one_line_example: GMP at ₹85 suggests a ~35% listing pop over issue price.

plain_english: A trade of ≥0.5% of a company's shares in a single day by one client — disclosed same-day by the exchange.
one_line_example: Bulk deal showed a marquee FII bought 1.2% — fresh institutional conviction.

plain_english: A single trade of ≥5 lakh shares or ₹10 cr+ in value, executed in a special morning window at exchange-approved price.
one_line_example: 3 cr shares crossed in a block deal at 2% below market.

plain_english: Profit as a percentage of revenue. Gross margin = (revenue − COGS) / revenue; operating margin adds in opex.
one_line_example: Operating margin expanded 150 bps — mix shifted toward premium products.

plain_english: Comparison versus the same period last year. Standard growth metric for quarterly earnings.
one_line_example: Revenue up 18% YoY but only 2% QoQ — growth decelerating.

plain_english: Comparison versus the previous quarter. Captures momentum better than YoY in volatile sectors.
one_line_example: QoQ margins dipped 80bps — near-term cost pressure.

plain_english: Annualized growth rate over a multi-year period, assuming compounding.
one_line_example: EPS CAGR of 22% over five years — compounding at work.

plain_english: Net profit divided by shareholder equity. How much profit the company generates on shareholders' capital.
one_line_example: 25% ROE with low leverage is a genuinely high-quality business.

plain_english: Operating profit divided by capital employed (equity + debt). Measures efficiency across the full capital base.
one_line_example: ROCE over 20% consistently is a durable-moat signal.

plain_english: Total debt divided by shareholders' equity — how leveraged the company is.
one_line_example: D/E ballooned from 0.3 to 1.4 after the acquisition — refinancing risk.

plain_english: Management's public forward-looking forecast for revenue, margin or other metrics.
one_line_example: Company cut FY guidance from 15% to 9% — stock gapped down 12%.

plain_english: The average analyst estimate. Beating consensus is typically bullish; missing it is bearish.
one_line_example: EPS of ₹22 vs consensus ₹20 — beat by 10%.

plain_english: When the market assigns a higher or lower P/E multiple to a stock, often after a structural change.
one_line_example: New management + margin expansion triggered a re-rating from 15× to 25×.

plain_english: Nifty futures traded outside Indian hours — first on SGX, now on GIFT-Nifty. Signals expected Nifty open.
one_line_example: GIFT Nifty up 80 pts — gap-up open expected.

plain_english: Registered foreign investor buying Indian equities/debt through the exchanges (same entity class as FII in most usage).
one_line_example: FPI flows turned net negative in September.
